# Architecture Vision: Verteiltes LLM- & Job-Execution-Cluster

**Version:** 1.0  
**Status:** Approved  
**Author:** Architect Agent  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Target System Shape
The system transforms idle workstation capacity (macOS and Windows laptops) into a distributed, containerized compute and LLM inference cluster for overnight batch processing. The target architecture maximizes code sharing across platforms via Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP), isolates all workloads within Docker containers, and maintains a strict separation of concerns across three core system tiers:
1. **Control Server (Ktor Backend):** Central coordinator for node registration, heartbeat monitoring, job scheduling, and metrics aggregation.
2. **Client Daemons (KMP Background Services):** Ultra-lightweight native services on macOS (LaunchDaemon) and Windows (Windows Service) that enforce keep-awake power assertions, sample system health telemetry, and interface with local Docker daemons.
3. **Admin Tool (Compose for Desktop):** Administrative desktop application providing real-time cluster monitoring, job execution inspection, and policy enforcement.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Admin Tool                         |
|         (Kotlin Multiplatform Desktop GUI)            |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
                            | REST / WebSockets (TLS)
                            v
+-------------------------------------------------------+
|                 Control Server                        |
|        (Ktor / Kotlin Multiplatform Backend)          |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
                            | REST / WebSockets (mTLS)
           +----------------+----------------+
           |                                 |
           v                                 v
+-----------------------+         +-----------------------+
|  macOS Client Daemon  |         | Windows Client Daemon |
|  (Background Service) |         |  (Background Service) |
+-----------+-----------+         +-----------+-----------+
            | Docker API                      | Docker API
            v                                 v
+-----------------------+         +-----------------------+
| Docker / Ollama / Ray |         | Docker / Ollama / Ray |
+-----------------------+         +-----------------------+\
```

---

## 2. Key Quality Attributes & Architectural Guardrails

### 2.1 Host Protection & Resource Footprint Guardrail
- **Idle Daytime Footprint:** When no batch jobs are running, the client daemon must consume < 1% CPU and < 50 MB resident memory (RSS).
- **Strict Isolation:** No job execution or untrusted script may run directly on the host OS. All compute jobs execute inside Docker containers with constrained CPU, memory, and networking limits.
- **Fail-Safe Power Management:** Host power assertions (`IOPMAssertionCreateWithName` on macOS, `SetThreadExecutionState` on Windows) must automatically release upon job completion, unexpected crash, or daemon shutdown to avoid draining laptop batteries unintentionally.

### 2.2 Communication & Security Guardrail
- **Mutual Authentication & Encryption:** All daemon-to-server and admin-to-server communications must run over TLS with mutual certificate authentication (mTLS) to prevent rogue node registration.
- **Heartbeat & Resiliency:** Nodes report telemetry every 15–30 seconds. A missing heartbeat for > 60 seconds triggers a node status transition to `Offline` and initiates automated job failover / re-dispatching.

### 2.3 Modularity & Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) Architecture
- **Shared Module (`:shared`):** Core domain models (`Node`, `Job`, `TelemetryMetrics`), protocol DTOs, validation logic, and serialization (`kotlinx.serialization`).
- **Server Module (`:server`):** Ktor server handling REST/WebSocket endpoints, node state store, job queue, and scheduler.
- **Client Daemon Module (`:daemon`):** Native targets for macOS (`macosArm64`, `macosX64`) and Windows (`mingwX64`), abstracting OS-level power assertions and Docker socket integrations through `expect`/`actual` declarations or common interfaces.
- **Admin Module (`:admin`):** Compose for Desktop application leveraging shared models.

---

## 3. Tech-Stack Guardrails

| Layer | Selected Technology | Architectural Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Language / Platform | Kotlin 2.x / Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) | Single language across backend, daemon, and UI; shared business logic and serialization schemas. |
| Server Framework | Ktor 3.x (CIO engine, Netty or Coroutine-based) | Lightweight, asynchronous, native coroutines support, low memory footprint. |
| Client Daemon Host Services | macOS LaunchDaemon / Windows Service | Non-intrusive autostart services operating with appropriate OS permissions for power management. |
| Container Runtime | Docker Engine via local Docker socket (`unix:///var/run/docker.sock` or Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\docker_engine`) | Broad ecosystem compatibility, standard image registries, robust resource isolation. |
| Distributed LLM / Workloads | Ray Core / Ollama container images | Ray provides distributed task scheduling and actor models; Ollama provides containerized GGUF inference. |
| Desktop UI | Jetpack Compose for Desktop | Modern declarative UI in Kotlin sharing viewmodels and models with `:shared`. |

---

## 4. Phase-by-Phase Roadmap Alignment

- **Phase 1 (MVP v0.1):** Core Ktor control server, KMP client daemon with host telemetry and power assertion (keep-awake), and Docker container execution runner. Validated on 5–10 devices.
- **Phase 2 (v0.2):** Distributed Ray/Ollama cluster integration for LLM coding agents, and Compose for Desktop admin monitoring.
- **Phase 3 (v0.3+):** Smart plug energy measuring (Shelly, Tapo) and advanced night-window scheduling policies.

product_backlog.title: Control Server Job Queue and Dispatcher
product_backlog.user_story: As an IT administrator or engineer, I want a central job queue and dispatching service on the Control Server, so that batch workloads are automatically routed and scheduled to eligible, available client nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Given submitted batch jobs in the Control Server queue, When active nodes with sufficient free capacity (CPU/RAM) are available, Then the server assigns the job to an eligible node.
Given an assigned job, When the node daemon accepts the job, Then the server transitions job state to Running.
Given a node failure or heartbeat timeout during an active job, When the node is marked Offline, Then the server reschedules or flags the job as Failed according to retry policy.

product_backlog.title: Control Server Node Registration & Heartbeat API
product_backlog.user_story: As a Control Server administrator, I want an API for node registration and periodic heartbeat telemetry, so that the server maintains an accurate real-time inventory of cluster nodes and their health.
acceptance_criteria: Given a running Ktor Control Server, When a client daemon sends a registration POST request with node ID, OS type, and hardware specs, Then the server stores the node and responds with 200 OK and registration confirmation.
Given a registered node, When the node sends a periodic heartbeat with CPU/RAM metrics, Then the server updates the node's last-seen timestamp and metric cache.
Given a registered node that stops sending heartbeats, When the timeout threshold (60 seconds) expires, Then the server marks the node status as Offline.
product_backlog.notes: Core registration and heartbeat telemetry for cluster nodes.
tasks: Set up Ktor server project structure and build configuration
Define NodeRegistrationRequest and HeartbeatTelemetry models
Implement NodeRegistry repository with TTL tracking
Implement registration and heartbeat API routes
Add automated tests for registration and timeout detection
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Control Server reliably tracks cluster node inventory and health status in real time.

product_backlog.title: Client Daemon & Power Management
product_backlog.description: Cross-platform background daemon for macOS and Windows that monitors system metrics, prevents standby during active workloads via power assertions, and executes tasks.

product_backlog.title: Docker Container Job Runner on Client Daemon
product_backlog.user_story: As a cluster job dispatcher, I want the client daemon to execute jobs inside isolated Docker containers and capture their lifecycle/logs, so that compute tasks execute cleanly and safely on heterogeneous client machines.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client daemon with Docker available, When the Control Server dispatches a job specification (image, env, command), Then the daemon pulls (if needed) and spawns an isolated container.
Given a running job container, When the container emits logs or exits, Then the daemon captures output and streams/reports status (Running, Succeeded, Failed) to the Control Server.
Given a stop command from the Control Server or a job completion, When cleanup is invoked, Then the container is stopped and removed without leaving orphaned processes.

product_backlog.title: Control Server & Node Orchestration
product_backlog.description: Ktor backend server managing client node registrations, telemetry, heartbeat health checks, and batch job scheduling across the cluster.

product_backlog.title: Containerized Job Execution
product_backlog.description: Isolated execution of computational tasks and AI jobs in Docker containers on client machines with resource controls.

product_backlog.title: Client Daemon Lifecycle & Metrics Collector
product_backlog.user_story: As a cluster administrator, I want a lightweight daemon running on client laptops that collects system metrics, so that the Control Server knows each node's capacity and current load.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client machine (macOS or Windows), When the daemon service starts at boot, Then it runs as a low-footprint background process consuming <1% CPU and <50MB RAM in idle.
Given a running daemon, When collecting system telemetry, Then it samples CPU usage, RAM utilization, battery charge level, and temperature, transmitting them via heartbeat.
tasks: Implement KMP platform daemon entry point for macOS (LaunchDaemon) and Windows Service
Implement platform-specific hardware metrics collectors (sysctl / OSHI)
Implement periodic reporting client to Control Server
Add unit tests for metrics serialization and collector thresholds
product_backlog.notes: Lightweight background daemon for cross-platform hardware monitoring.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Client nodes reliably report system resource availability without impacting normal daytime laptop usability.

product_backlog.title: Client Daemon Power Assertion and Sleep Prevention
product_backlog.user_story: As a cluster operator, I want client daemons to assert OS power locks (keep-awake) during active workloads, so that overnight compute jobs run to completion without machines falling asleep.
acceptance_criteria: Given a macOS client running an active batch job or keep-awake instruction, When idle timeout triggers, Then IOPMAssertionCreateWithName prevents the system from going to sleep.
Given a Windows client running an active batch job or keep-awake instruction, When idle timeout triggers, Then SetThreadExecutionState prevents the system from entering sleep.
Given an active job that completes or is cancelled, When the daemon releases the keep-awake assertion, Then the OS resumes normal power management and sleep timers.

Cluster Admin Dashboard & Policy Management
product_backlog.description: Compose for Desktop management application for cluster operators to observe nodes, submit jobs, and enforce execution policies.

product_backlog.title: Distributed LLM & Ray Inference Engine
product_backlog.description: Distributed inference framework connecting idle cluster nodes using Ray and Ollama to host and run open-source coding LLMs.

product_backlog.title: Admin Dashboard Node Status and Live Metrics View
product_backlog.user_story: As an IT Administrator, I want a desktop dashboard displaying registered cluster nodes and real-time telemetry, so that I can observe cluster capacity and health at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: Given an active Control Server with registered nodes, When an administrator opens the Admin Dashboard, Then the dashboard displays all registered nodes with their online/offline status and OS type.
Given active nodes sending periodic heartbeats, When node telemetry updates on the server, Then the dashboard reflects current CPU usage, RAM utilization, and battery state.
Given a node marked offline due to heartbeat timeout, When viewed in the dashboard, Then the node is highlighted with an offline badge and last-seen timestamp.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Client machines can form a unified Ray cluster to run parallelized distributed computing tasks.
product_backlog.description: As a cluster administrator, I want client nodes to automatically join a distributed Ray cluster as worker nodes when instructed by the Control Server, so that distributed compute tasks can execute across idle machines.
product_backlog.title: Distributed Ray Cluster Bootstrap on Client Nodes
product_backlog.notes: Enables distributed computing across heterogeneous Apple Silicon and Windows nodes via Ray.
tasks: Define RayWorkerConfig schema and launch arguments
Implement Ray worker container orchestration in daemon
Add health check and clean shutdown handling for Ray workers
Add integration test for worker container lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Given a client daemon instructed to join the Ray cluster, When the daemon receives cluster head coordinates, Then it launches a containerized Ray worker connecting to the specified head.
Given a running Ray worker container, When the client node status changes to busy or disconnects, Then the worker cleanly leaves the Ray cluster.
product_backlog.user_story: As a cluster administrator, I want client nodes to automatically join a distributed Ray cluster as worker nodes when instructed by the Control Server, so that distributed compute tasks can execute across idle machines.

tasks: Create OllamaRunner client in daemon codebase
Implement model pull and readiness verification check
Expose proxy inference endpoint with streaming response support
Add integration test with lightweight test model
product_backlog.notes: Executes open coding LLMs locally on client hardware via Ollama.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client daemon with Docker support, When instructed to prepare an Ollama model, Then it ensures the Ollama container is running and initiates pulling the target model tag.

Given a loaded Ollama model, When an inference prompt request is forwarded to the client daemon, Then the local Ollama API generates the completion response and returns metrics (tokens/sec, total tokens).
product_backlog.user_story: As a developer running LLM coding agents, I want client nodes to pull designated Ollama models and execute local inference workloads, so that code analysis tasks run directly on idle client hardware.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Client nodes can execute LLM coding queries locally, eliminating central cloud inference costs.
product_backlog.title: Ollama Model Runner and Local Inference Execution

acceptance_criteria: Given the Compose for Desktop Admin Dashboard, When the admin enters job parameters (docker image, command, target node tags) and clicks Submit, Then the job is posted to the Control Server and appears in the active queue table.
Given active running jobs in the cluster, When the admin views the Job Pipeline view, Then each job's live state (Queued, Running, Succeeded, Failed) and execution duration are dynamically updated.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Operators can dispatch jobs and monitor progress through an intuitive desktop GUI without CLI scripting.
tasks: Build Job Submission form view in Compose for Desktop
Connect form to POST /api/jobs Control Server endpoint
Build Job Pipeline data table with status indicators
Add unit tests for Job Submission ViewModel
product_backlog.notes: Provides visual workflow control for dispatching and tracking cluster jobs.
product_backlog.title: Admin Dashboard Job Submission and Status Pipeline View
product_backlog.user_story: As an IT administrator, I want a Compose for Desktop UI to submit batch job configurations and view active job progress in real time, so that I can manage and monitor cluster workload execution.

acceptance_criteria: Given a scheduled batch job and a night-time execution window (e.g., 22:00 to 06:00), When the current time is outside the allowed window, Then the dispatcher holds the job in Queued state without assigning it to nodes.

Given a running job on a battery-powered client node, When battery level drops below 50% or CPU temperature exceeds 85°C, Then the daemon signals the Control Server, pauses or evicts the job container, and relinquishes the power assertion.
product_backlog.title: Night-Time Scheduling Windows and Thermal Guard Policy
tasks: Define ClusterPolicy schema (time windows, battery floor, thermal ceiling)
Implement policy validation in Control Server dispatcher
Implement hardware guard checks in client daemon heartbeat loop
Add unit tests for policy evaluations and threshold triggers
product_backlog.notes: Protects hardware integrity and guarantees zero interference during normal working hours.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Automated policy enforcement prevents battery degradation and overheating during unattended overnight runs.
product_backlog.user_story: As a system operator, I want to enforce strict night-time execution windows and pause jobs when battery falls below 50% or thermal throttling occurs, so that client hardware is protected and daytime work is undisturbed.

product_backlog.title: Smart Plug Energy Monitoring
product_backlog.description: Integration with Shelly and Tapo smart plugs to record actual electrical energy consumption and attribute wattage/kWh per job.

product_backlog.user_story: As an energy efficiency researcher, I want the Control Server to collect real-time wattage data from smart plugs connected to client laptops, so that energy consumption during jobs is accurately monitored.
product_backlog.title: Smart Plug Telemetry Collector for Shelly and Tapo
tasks: Implement SmartPlugClient interface with Shelly and Tapo adapters
Create SmartPlugManager service with periodic polling loop
Add node-to-plug configuration mapping schema
Add mock API tests for Shelly and Tapo response parsing
product_backlog.notes: Integrates external smart plug hardware telemetry into the cluster control plane.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Real-time energy measurements provide empirical ground-truth power data for laptop clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a configured smart plug IP and credentials (Shelly Gen2 / Tapo P110), When the Control Server queries the smart plug API, Then it successfully reads instantaneous power (Watts) and cumulative energy (kWh).
Given mapped smart plugs to node IDs, When power metrics are collected periodically, Then the Control Server records timestamped power telemetry in the node metrics store.

product_backlog.notes: Attributes measured physical energy costs directly to individual batch compute workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed job run with start and end timestamps and an assigned node, When the job completes, Then the Control Server computes the integrated energy consumption (kWh) over the job duration from the smart plug metrics.

Given computed job energy metrics, When the admin requests job execution details via the API or dashboard, Then the total energy consumed (kWh) and average power draw (W) are returned in the job report.
tasks: Implement energy integration calculator (trapezoidal rule over wattage timeseries)
Store job energy summary in JobResult entity
Expose GET /api/jobs/{id}/energy endpoint in Control Server
Add unit test validating energy calculation against known wattage traces
product_backlog.user_story: As an administrator, I want the Control Server to correlate smart plug energy data with individual job runs, so that the total kilowatt-hour cost of batch LLM inference jobs can be analyzed and reported.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Enables transparent cost and carbon footprint attribution for AI workloads running on idle hardware.
product_backlog.title: Energy Consumption Correlation and Reporting per Job
